Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Document-level:
- Certificate number: R76/1992-NL1-10.07
- Scheme: This is R76 scheme... The "scheme" field per schema is (A|B). Hmm, for OIML-CS, scheme A or B. The cert doesn't explicitly mention scheme A or B. It's from 2010, issued by NMi Certin under OIML-CS? The certificate number format "R76/1992-NL1-10.07" — this is a national OIML certificate, pre-dating the OIML-CS scheme designation. I'll omit scheme or set null. Actually rule 8 says don't fabricate. The scheme field is in the schema as certificate.scheme (A|B). Not mentioned, so omit.

- project_number: 10200194
- page_total: 2
- member_state: The Netherlands
- date_issued: 18 March 2010 → 2010-03-18

- name: NMi Certin B.V.

Manufacturer:
- same

Certified type:
- category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — the schema examples say "Load cell", "Indicator", etc. Category here is Non-automatic weighing instrument (NAWI). I'll use "Non-automatic weighing instrument".
- type_designations: MS21-NEOV…, MS-235…, MS-2504…, MS-2515…, MS-383…, MS-391…, MS-464…, MS-491…, MS-573…, MS-544…, MS-584…, MBF-59…

The "…" indicates family suffixes. I'll record the designations as given. Should I keep the ellipsis "…"? Yes, they're part of the designation pattern. Use the Unicode ellipsis or three dots? The markdown shows "…". I'll keep "…".

- module_designation: null (not applicable; it's a complete instrument). Actually the cert mentions indicator DP-3700 and load cells as tested components. The "Identification of certified type" doesn't give module designation. I could set module_designation to null and omit.

- description: Maybe combine: "n ≤ 6000 for class III instruments with single interval indication..." Actually those are characteristics. Let me put them in characteristics config_level since they vary by configuration (class and indication type).

Characteristics:
- n (number of verification intervals) varies by configuration:
  - class III, single interval: n ≤ 6000 → max 6000
  - class III, multi-interval: n ≤ 3000 → max 3000
  - class IIII, single interval: n ≤ 1000 → max 1000
- max partial weighing ranges: 2
- temperature range: +5 °C / +35 °C → {min: 5, max: 35}, unit °C

config_level entries:
- attribute: "max_verification_intervals", axis: "accuracy_class_and_indication", values: [{condition: "class III, single interval indication", value: 6000}, {condition: "class III, multi-interval indication", value: 3000}, {condition: "class IIII, single interval indication", value: 1000}]
- attribute "maximum_partial_weighing_ranges": value 2 — that's type_level.
- temperature_range: type_level: {min: 5, max: 35}, unit °C.

Model family: The cert covers multiple type designations (12 types). Are these model variants? They're type designations with "..." suffix patterns, meaning families. Should I create model_family? Rule 4 says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are 12 type designations. But no attributes vary per model in the markdown. Hmm. The instruction: "model_family: include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". There are 12 models. But there's no per-model attribute matrix. I could include model_family with models listed as model_id for each type designation. That seems reasonable. But family_name? Not given, null.

Actually, is it a family? The types share the certificate. I'll include model_family with the 12 model IDs. But wait — no model_level characteristics exist. It's fine to include models without attributes. Hmm, but rule 8 says don't fabricate; listing models is not fabrication since they're in the doc.

Actually, let me reconsider: the type designations include "…" suffix meaning variants within each type. Listing each as a model_id with the ellipsis seems fine.

Recommendation:
- id: "R76", edition: 1992, amendment: null, accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]

Test reports: The cert lists test reports and referenced certificates. The schema: test_reports[] with id, date, pages, role. Roles: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report.

The listed items:
For the indicator (DP-3700):
- 812493A, 44 pages
- 812493B, 16 pages
- 9200569, 19 pages

For the load cell (referenced R60 certificates):
- Tedea 1022, 1022P, LPS: R60/1991-NL-96.03 (37 pages), R60/1991-NL-96.05 (35), R60/2000-NL1-04.02A (38), R60/2000-NL1-04.02B (8), R60/2000-NL1-04.02C (37)
- Tedea 1242: R60/1991-NL-99.10 (38), R60/1991-NL-00.05 (38), R60/2000-NL1-03.09 (38)
- Tedea 380, 380W: R60/2000-NL1-10.01A (62), R60/2000-NL1-10.01B (61)
- Zemic L6E3: 2004-WJ-0047 (18), 2005-WJ-0028 (17)

These referenced R60 certificates — are they test reports? They're type approval certificates for load cells, referenced as supporting documentation. I'll list them as test_reports with role "type_evaluation_report" or "test_report"? The doc says "The conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated Test Reports". So all these are associated test reports. The indicator ones (812493A etc.) are test reports. The load cell ones are actually R60 certificates — but they serve as test evidence. I'll mark indicator ones as "test_report" and load cell ones as "type_evaluation_report"? Hmm, they are referenced certificates. Maybe role "test_report" for all since the text calls them Test Reports. Actually the load cell items are certificates (N° R60/...). I'd use role "test_report" for all to be simple, but the distinction might matter. The schema roles: type_evaluation_report, test_report, documentation_file, evaluation_report. For R60 certificates used as evidence, "test_report" is closest since they contain test results. I'll use "test_report" for all.

Also mentioned: "the type-approval certificate and the description with number T7614 and the appertaining documentation folder". T7614 is a documentation number (description). Should that be a test_report with role documentation_file? Yes: {"id": "T7614", "role": "documentation_file"}. Pages unknown. Date unknown.

Components: The cert names indicator DP-3700 and load cells Tedea 1022, 1022P, LPS, 1242, 380, 380W, Zemic L6E3. These are sub-assemblies of the weighing instruments. Should I record components[]? Rule 6: "For complex instruments... record each as a components[] entry". The test reports section names indicator and load cells. These are indeed components of the NAWI. I'll include:

components:
- role: "indicator", type_designations: ["DP-3700"]
- role: "load cell", type_designations: ["Tedea 1022", "Tedea 1022P", "Tedea LPS", "Tedea 1242", "Tedea 380", "Tedea 380W", "Zemic L6E3"], alternatives: "OR"? The cert lists different load cell types used — these are alternatives (any of these may be used). I'd set alternatives: "OR" for the load cell component? The load cells: "Tedea type 1022, 1022P and LPS" — "and" there, but overall the instrument may use any of the listed. Hmm. I could have separate component entries per manufacturer group:

- {role: "load cell", type_designations: ["1022", "1022P", "LPS"], manufacturer: Tedea...} — schema doesn't have manufacturer in components. characteristics{} allowed.

I'll do:
components: [
  {role: "Indicator", type_designations: ["DP-3700"]},
  {role: "Load cell", type_designations: ["Tedea 1022", "Tedea 1022P", "Tedea LPS", "Tedea 1242", "Tedea 380", "Tedea 380W", "Zemic L6E3"], alternatives: "OR"}
]

That seems reasonable.

"u:degree_Celsius" — the example in the schema shows "u:degree_Celsius" as a valid unitsdb ID. I'm fairly confident unitsdb has u:degree_Celsius. The instruction example lists `"unit_id": "u:degree_Celsius" | null`. I'll use it for °C. For intervals count (n), dimensionless — unit null.

Add description for the documentation? Schema fields: id, date, pages, role. Could I add a "note"? Not in schema — but adding extra fields? Better to stick to schema. Use "..." (three ASCII dots) or "…" (single char)? The markdown shows "…" (U+2026). I'll use "…".
